html:
The first attempt to count the whole population of British India, carried out between 1867 and 1872 under the viceroy Lord Mayo. It counted about 200 million people under British rule.

It was not done on one day across the country; different provinces counted at different times. The first true all-India census on a single date came in 1881, and India has held one every ten years since. Counting people was an old practice in large states, as the Han census of China shows, but the British census went further in what it asked.

Besides age, sex and occupation, it recorded each person's religion and caste. This had lasting effects. Officials sorted thousands of local groups into fixed categories, and later censuses tried to rank castes in order of status. Groups petitioned to be listed higher. Many historians argue that the census made caste and religious identity more rigid and more political, a legacy that shaped the Partition of India and later quota politics such as the Mandal Commission.

In 2023 India became the most populous country in the world.
sum: The first attempt to count the whole population of British India, carried out between 1867 and 1872 under the viceroy Lord Mayo. It counted about 200 million people under British rule.
